purpose: Ubrogepant is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It is taken when a migraine starts to help relieve the pain and other symptoms like nausea and sensitivity to light or sound. It is not used every day to prevent migraines — only when you actually get one.
how_it_works: During a migraine, your body releases a substance called CGRP that causes pain and inflammation in the brain. Ubrogepant blocks the place where CGRP attaches, which stops it from triggering migraine pain. Think of it like putting a lock cover over a keyhole so the key cannot get in.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea and sleepiness or feeling tired. Most people tolerate it well, but let your doctor know if these bother you.
warnings: Do not take ubrogepant if you are also taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole or clarithromycin, as this combination can cause dangerously high levels of the drug in your body. Tell your doctor about all your medications, including herbal supplements. It should be used with caution if you have severe liver or kidney problems. Avoid taking it with grapefruit juice. It is not recommended during pregnancy unless clearly needed, so talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 50 mg or 100 mg taken by mouth as soon as your migraine starts. If your migraine comes back or does not fully go away, you can take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first dose. Do not take more than 200 mg total in any 24-hour period.
